finding.claim: SQL injection via unvalidated ORDER BY parameter in list_users_sorted. The attacker-controlled `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query. ORDER BY cannot be parameterized, and there is no allowlist. An attacker can use boolean/blind subqueries or CASE expressions to exfiltrate data from any table in the SQLite DB (e.g. other users' columns, password hashes).
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: concatenated into the SQL string and executed with PDO::query, with no escaping or allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No auth, no allowlist, no casting in the function. The sibling list_users_safe (list.php:10-12) uses an allowlist map, which shows the unsafe version lacks it. find_user uses a prepared statement and is not vulnerable. Only the entry point is this file, and no middleware exists in the directory. Repro: ?sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users LIMIT 1)='a' THEN id ELSE name END). Stacked queries are generally not allowed in PDO sqlite query(), but blind exfiltration works.

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted; the allowlist exists only in list_users_safe (list.php:10-11), and find_user uses a prepared statement (list.php:16)
verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] straight into the ORDER BY clause of a PDO::query call with no allowlist, cast or auth, so an anonymous caller can inject subqueries or CASE expressions. Caveats: list.php is the only file in the directory and nothing calls list_users_sorted, and the `password` column in the repro is assumed because no schema is present.
